result.goal: Crewed Mun landing and return: land Jebediah on the Mun, plant a flag, bring him home. MechJeb flies the ascent; ASTRA's own powered-descent reflex lands.
relevant_lessons: - [2026-06-27] (landing) Mun terminal-descent failures: a fixed 30 m suicide-burn margin forced near-full throttle near the ground (bounce, drift, dry tanks); a capped hover from 250 m oscillated and burned the return fuel; lateral cleanup starting at 120 m with 7.5 m/s sideways was too late (impact at 18.8 m/s); switching to vertical while drifting preserved the slide. Null the horizontal speed before contact and stay retrograde until it is small.

- [2026-06-27] (landing, design) A lander engine enclosed by its own interstage shroud had its exhaust blocked: full throttle, fuel draining, g-force 0 (an LV-N at trans-Mun injection). Engines that stay attached must have bare bells.

- [2026-06-27] (landing) The airless hoverslam that worked on the Mun: coast until surface speed reaches v_ref(h) = √(2(f·a_max − g)h) with ~8% thrust reserve (f ≈ 0.92), then track the curve surface-retrograde; below ~70 m the curve is too steep to track, so a separate terminal controller is needed. Best touchdown: −0.1 m/s vertical, 0.2 m/s horizontal.

- [2026-06-27] (mechjeb, landing, warp) MechJeb's landing autopilot will not fast-warp a long descent ellipse from a high orbit (~9,400 km apoapsis); warp-assist down to near the top of the atmosphere, then hand control back.

- [2026-06-27] (mechjeb, landing, reentry) MechJeb's landing autopilot owns deorbit, attitude, braking, and chute timing and beat every hand-rolled descent, but from a stable orbit above the atmosphere (a 62 km Duna circle) it never deorbited, and a held SAS retrograde fights it. Put the periapsis into the lower atmosphere yourself, release SAS, then engage.

- [2026-06-27] (mechjeb, staging, capture) MechJeb's StagingController is separate from the ascent autostage flag: the landing autopilot and an autostaging ascent leave it active, and it autostages during ANY later burn. It fired a heat-shield/payload decoupler mid-capture and stranded a crew pod at Eve with no engine, shield, or chutes. Release it before every in-space burn.

- [2026-06-27] (landing, burns) Deorbiting from a too-high Mun orbit with a guessed retrograde attitude raised the periapsis twice; lower the apoapsis first with a computed node, then deorbit at apoapsis. Large lowering burns need full throttle: a 0.18 throttle cap timed out.

- [2026-06-27] (landing, design, eva) A tall, narrow single-stack lander tipped over on Duna, burying the hatch and blocking both the flag and the ascent. Design for a tip-over angle well above the expected slopes (wide stance, low centre of mass) and check tilt before any surface ignition.

args.text: Design ASTRA Mun Lander 1 from the live catalog: Mainsail core 3673 m/s, Terrier transfer stage 1848 m/s, Terrier lander 2010 m/s (vacuum). Budget: ascent ~3400, trans-Mun ~860, capture ~300, landing+ascent ~1300, return ~300. MechJeb flies the ascent with auto-staging limited to stage 3.

args.summary: Jebediah landed on the Mun (Midlands, 0.26 S 168.77 E), planted the flag 'ASTRA Mun Base 1', and splashed down at 4.4 m/s. MechJeb flew the ascent and trans-Mun injection; ASTRA's fly_descent landed at 1.5 m/s on the third attempt after two guidance fixes (broken Mk1-pod bounding box; terrain ahead). The narrow lander tipped over twice on a 5.7 deg slope: the next lander needs a wider stance.
